newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU says plans to propose airport slot resale.
newsitem.headline: EU says plans to propose airport slot resale.

text.p: The European Commission is planning to allow airlines to buy and sell their landing and take-off slots at EU airports but will not introduce wholesale auctions of all slots, officials said on Thursday.

Plans under discussion within the EU executive, if adpoted, would leave intact the existing twice-yearly share-out of new or unused slots at airports while legalising the so-called secondary market for airlines wishing to sell the slots they already have, a Commission spokeswoman told reporters.
"In terms of the primary market, we do not have very much to say," the spokeswoman said on the margins of an EU transport ministers meeting in Luxembourg.
"The way we would like to proceed is to tighten up safeguards in the primary market and, where there is a secondary market, to make that absolutely transparent," the official said.
This would clear up the so-called grey market in slots which the Commission fears benefits bigger airlines by allowing them to build up dominant positions unofficially.

The spokeswoman denied the work came as a result of investigations by Britain's Office of Fair Trading into the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines, saying the review had been planned long before that deal was announced earlier this year.
